title: Verb position in main clauses (V2)
summary: In a main clause the conjugated verb is always the second element.
explanation: The first element can be the subject or something else, such as a time word. The verb stays in second place, and the subject moves behind it when something else comes first.

examples.note: Time word first, verb still second

title: Nominative and accusative articles
summary: The subject takes the nominative; the direct object takes the accusative.
explanation: Only the masculine article changes between the two cases: der becomes den, and ein becomes einen. Feminine, neuter and plural forms stay the same.

title: Two-way prepositions (Wechselpräpositionen)
summary: Nine prepositions take accusative for motion and dative for location.
explanation: Ask 'Wohin?' (where to?) for motion, which takes the accusative. Ask 'Wo?' (where?) for location, which takes the dative.

examples.german: Ich lege das Buch auf den Tisch.
examples.english: I put the book on the table.

examples.german: Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch.
examples.english: The book is lying on the table.
